subject: Biotechnology
title: RNA Therapeutics Beyond Vaccines
description: A quick win: understand RNA Therapeutics Beyond Vaccines.

hook.text: mRNA is not just for vaccines — Onpattro uses RNA interference to silence a disease gene in the liver.

buildup.text: Small interfering RNA binds messenger RNA and triggers its destruction — no protein is made from the silenced gene.

discovery.text: Onpattro treats hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis — silencing the faulty TTR gene stops toxic protein buildup.

twist.text: Antisense oligonucleotides work differently — they bind pre-mRNA to modify splicing or block translation.

climax.text: Inclisiran lowers cholesterol with two injections per year — siRNA against PCSK9 lasts for months per dose.

punchline.text: Silence the gene, stop the disease — RNA drugs rewrite pharmacology.

quiz.question: How does RNA interference silence a gene?
options: It edits the DNA sequence to remove the gene permanently
Small interfering RNA binds and triggers destruction of the target messenger RNA
It blocks ribosomes from attaching to any messenger RNA

details.summary: RNA therapeutics extend beyond vaccines to include mRNA-encoded proteins, siRNA gene silencing, antisense oligonucleotides, and RNA editing. These approaches can target previously undruggable disease mechanisms by intervening at the RNA level rather than protein level.
details.whyItMatters: RNA therapeutics unlock targets unreachable by antibodies or small molecules. By intervening before proteins are made, they can silence disease-causing genes, encode missing proteins, or edit RNA sequences, vastly expanding the druggable genome.
takeaways: RNA therapeutics include mRNA, siRNA, antisense, and RNA editing approaches
They can target disease mechanisms unreachable by conventional drugs
The RNA therapeutics market is projected to grow exponentially through 2030

faq.question: How does siRNA silence specific genes?
faq.answer: Small interfering RNA binds to complementary messenger RNA and recruits the RISC complex to chop it up, preventing protein production. This silences specific genes for weeks per dose. Patisiran, approved for hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis, was the first siRNA drug.

faq.question: What diseases can RNA therapeutics treat that other drugs cannot?
faq.answer: RNA therapies can target transcription factors, non-coding RNAs, and proteins inside cells that antibodies cannot reach. Approved treatments address spinal muscular atrophy, hereditary amyloidosis, and hypercholesterolemia; trials target Huntington's disease and other intractable conditions.
